enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

saml.description: A SAML source can be configured to allow IdP-initiated logins, which the documentation warns may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified and could authenticate a user without interaction.
saml.note: If this option is enabled, acceptance of unsolicited SAML responses is by configuration and should not be reported as a generic vulnerability.

saml.description: When a Source stage invokes a source flow, having a User Login stage bound in that source flow causes direct authentication instead of resuming the original flow.
saml.note: This can look like broken flow atomicity, but it is documented behavior of Source stage composition.

saml.description: Policies on stage bindings may be evaluated when the flow is planned or when the stage is run, producing different outcomes as context changes during the flow.
saml.note: Different results before and after context changes can be expected depending on binding evaluation mode.

saml.description: If a Source stage resume timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning when the user returns from the external source.
saml.note: Mid-flow restarts after timeout are expected behavior, not session confusion.

saml.description: When an OAuth/OIDC client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
saml.note: Extra claims in tokens/userinfo after an empty-scope request are by design and should not be flagged as over-granting.

saml.description: Applications are accessible to all users when no bindings are defined.
saml.note: Broad access without bindings is by design and should not be reported as authorization escalation.

saml.description: Using email address as SAML NameID is discouraged because users are free to change email addresses by default.
saml.note: Identity changes following email changes are expected when email-based NameID is configured.

saml.description: NameID generation is configurable and may use hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, transient session ID, or email address.
saml.note: Identity comparisons must account for the configured NameID policy; mutable or transient identifiers can change by design.

saml.description: SAML source can allow IdP-initiated logins, and the documentation warns that this request is not verified and may constitute a security risk.
saml.note: A successful unsolicited SAML login in this mode is documented behavior and should not automatically be reported as a signature-validation bug.

saml.description: As of authentik 2025.10, the email scope mapping defaults email_verified to false because authentik has no authoritative verification source.
saml.note: Do not treat email_verified=false as a broken identity mapping; it is the documented secure default.

saml.description: RP-initiated logout uses default-provider-invalidation-flow, which by default does not include User Logout, so the authentik session remains active.
saml.note: A surviving authentik session after application logout is by design unless full single logout was explicitly configured.

saml.constraint: SAML source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is a security-sensitive toggle. For SP-request-bound tests (especially I3 flow coherence and request correlation), the fuzzer MUST keep IdP-initiated logins disabled unless it is explicitly testing that insecure mode. Enabling it removes the requirement for prior SP interaction and can make unsolicited assertions succeed by design.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature-validation tests against authentik as SP, the fuzzer MUST create/use a SAML Source with default settings unless documentation explicitly states signature validation is enabled by default. The docs warn that allowing IdP-initiated logins may accept unverified requests; a successful unsolicited SAML login in that mode is not proof of signature bypass unless the test is specifically targeting that insecure configuration.

For I1/I3 SAML flow tests, saml_login MUST be executed as an SP-initiated flow using the ACS endpoint and a matching in-response flow context. authentik flow execution is session/context based, and SAML/OAuth source stages suspend and later resume flows. Sending a bare unsolicited ACS POST without initiating the flow can fail for flow-state reasons unrelated to the security property under test.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, include a CONTROL login first with a valid assertion to confirm the source and flow are configured correctly. A failed replay attempt is only meaningful if the same environment accepts a fresh valid assertion.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, include a CONTROL login without expired_assertion=true before the expired attempt. Otherwise a rejection cannot be distinguished from broken source configuration, missing flow state, or unrelated SAML parsing failure.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving source stages, authentik resumes suspended flows only if the source flow does not contain a User Login stage. If the source authentication/enrollment flow has a User Login stage bound, the source flow authenticates directly instead of resuming the original flow. Do NOT interpret this by-design control-flow change as a session-binding vulnerability.

For I3 config-change sequences, authentik evaluates some policies dynamically at stage run time by default, but stage bindings can be configured to 'Evaluate when flow is planned', which caches decisions into the flow plan. A valid coherence test MUST hold this setting constant and distinguish stale planned-flow behavior from normal re-evaluation semantics.

For I3 tests that rely on source-stage resume timing, the Source stage has a configurable 'Resume timeout'. If the timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning by design. Do NOT treat restart-after-timeout as a flow coherence bug.

For I4 identity-binding tests on SAML, NameID format materially changes the identifier value. authentik may derive NameID from hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, session ID, or email depending on NameID policy. The fuzzer MUST keep NameID policy fixed across compared logins; otherwise identity changes are expected configuration behavior, not principal-collision evidence.

For I4 tests involving email-based identity, avoid using the SAML NameID email-address policy as the sole stable identifier unless the test intentionally targets email binding. The docs explicitly warn that users may change email addresses, so email-based NameID is not a stable principal by design.

For I4/I5 group and attribute mapping tests, authentik SAML property mappings are arbitrary expressions and default mappings can be removed. The fuzzer MUST verify which mappings are enabled before asserting missing/present attributes as security outcomes; absent attributes may simply reflect provider/source mapping configuration.

For I5 authorization tests using OAuth/OIDC verification after SAML-based upstream login, authentik's OAuth provider treats a request with no scopes as requesting all configured scopes. The fuzzer MUST explicitly request minimal scopes when testing over-granting; omitting scope broadens claims by design and can create false positives.

For I5 tests involving email_verified, authentik versions prior to 2025.10 set email_verified=True for the email scope by default, while 2025.10+ defaults it to False. The fuzzer MUST record platform version/behavior before treating email_verified=true as an authorization-binding issue.

For revocation/introspection-based freshness tests, authentik's introspection endpoint can only introspect a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless the token is first exchanged for one from that provider. The fuzzer MUST use matching provider context or token exchange; otherwise introspection failure is expected and not evidence of invalid token state.

For refresh/session lifetime tests, User Login stage 'Session duration' uses a sentinel where seconds=0 means the session expires on browser close, not an already-expired session. Do NOT treat 0 as literal zero lifetime.

For MFA freshness tests, Authenticator Validation stage 'Last validation threshold' uses a sentinel where zero means validate every time. Non-zero values relax MFA prompts. Additionally, for code-based devices values lower than seconds=30 cannot be used precisely. Do NOT assume sub-30-second thresholds provide exact enforcement semantics.

For email-based authenticator tests, 'Token Expiration' is configured in minutes and defaults to 30. The fuzzer SHOULD vary this explicitly when testing freshness rather than assuming a shorter default.

SAML source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For I1/I3/I5 SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish SP-initiated ACS testing from IdP-initiated login mode; enabling IdP-initiated logins can make forged or unsolicited assertions succeed by design and would create false positives.

For all SAML ACS tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve request binding state (InResponseTo/RelayState) before posting the forged SAMLResponse. The docs describe authentik as an SP with ACS at /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ and the profile requires SP-initiated flow context; sending a standalone fabricated response without initiating flow will be rejected for flow-state reasons, not because signature/issuer/audience checks worked.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, the fuzzer MUST account for the documented 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' insecurity separately from signature validation. A successful forged SAMLResponse can be caused by unsolicited-login acceptance rather than trust-anchor extraction bugs; keep IdP-initiated mode disabled unless that specific behavior is under test.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure the SAML source with an explicit upstream Issuer/Entity ID. The docs expose 'Issuer/Entity ID' as a source setting; if it is unset or loosely configured, issuer comparison may be skipped or ambiguous, causing a trivial pass/fail unrelated to issuer validation.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, use the same Assertion/@ID across both saml_login events and keep all other flow inputs stable. authentik acts as an SP consuming assertions at the ACS endpoint, so replay detection must be evaluated on the exact same assertion identity; changing IDs invalidates the replay oracle.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control SAML login first using a non-expired assertion. Without a control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from generic SAML source misconfiguration, missing SP-initiated state, or disabled source visibility in the Identification stage.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving source-stage or external-source authentication, do NOT treat resumed-flow timeout expiry as a security failure. The Source stage documents a 'Resume timeout' after which the suspended flow restarts from the beginning; inconsistent outcomes across requests that cross this timeout are by design, not stale-session bugs.

For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, ensure the compared paths use the same effective flow semantics. authentik flows can inject or skip stages dynamically based on bindings and policies, and Source stage documentation warns that source authentication/enrollment flows must not contain a User Login stage or they will authenticate directly instead of resuming the original flow. A valid bypass test must show the alternate SAML path skipping MFA for the same principal, not merely using a differently configured flow.

For I4 email-linking and account-collision tests, do not assume NameID is the stable binding key. The docs state NameID policy is configurable and may be persistent hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, transient session ID, or email address. The fuzzer MUST record which NameID policy is configured before interpreting merges/collisions; email-based NameID and transient NameID can change identity semantics by design.

For I4 tests targeting email-based collisions, if the SAML source/provider is configured to use Email address NameID, the docs explicitly warn that users may change email addresses. Apparent account merges or rebinding caused by mutable email identifiers are configuration-risk behavior; only flag a violation when the platform links principals contrary to the configured identifier policy, not merely because email was chosen as the identifier.

For I4 multi-identity tests, avoid using transient NameID policy when you need stable cross-login identity comparison. The docs state transient NameID is based on the user's session ID, so repeated logins can legitimately produce different identifiers and confound collision or merge oracles.

For I5 SAML audience/conditions tests, use assertions that differ only in Conditions/AudienceRestriction while keeping the rest of the assertion valid. The ACS glossary explicitly states the SP validates signatures, issuer, audience, and time conditions before creating a session; missing SP-initiated state or malformed assertions will mask whether audience/conditions enforcement actually occurred.

For OAuth/OIDC verification steps used after SAML-based login, remember that authentik's token endpoint returns access_token and optionally id_token, but session_token for subsequent API calls MUST be the access_token. Using id_token against /application/o/userinfo/ will fail for protocol reasons and create false negatives in post-login verification.

When testing scope/authorization binding on authentik's OAuth endpoints, a request with no scopes is treated as requesting all configured scopes. Therefore the fuzzer MUST explicitly request a minimal scope set when checking for over-granting; omitting scope broadens access by design and will create false positives for I5.

For refresh-token or long-lived-session assumptions, note that starting with authentik 2024.2 applications only receive a refresh token when both the application and the request include offline_access. Do not interpret absence of refresh_token as revocation or freshness enforcement unless offline_access was explicitly configured and requested.

For all SAML freshness tests on authentik's SAML source (saml_expired_assertion, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_one_time_use_replay), the sequence MUST include a control SAML login first using the same source configuration but without the attack mutation. Otherwise a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken source setup or flow misconfiguration.

SAML Source 'NameID Policy' is an exact enumerated format selector, not a wildcard or pattern-matching field. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT treat it as a subject constraint and MUST NOT attempt wildcard values; choose a concrete NameID format or omit reliance on NameID-policy-based filtering entirely.

If a SAML source is embedded through a Source stage, the configured source authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. Documentation states this prevents resuming the original flow and directly authenticates the pending user instead. For I3 flow-coherence tests, avoid Source-stage compositions with source flows that include User Login, or results will reflect by-design flow short-circuiting rather than a coherence bug.

Flow-stage policy timing matters in authentik. Policies can be evaluated either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. For I3 config-change or mid-flow coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this: a policy result cached at plan time is by design if 'Evaluate when flow is planned' is enabled. A valid I3 finding must show inconsistent handling of the same request under the same evaluation mode, not expected differences between plan-time and run-time evaluation.

User Login stage 'Session duration' uses a sentinel where seconds=0 means the session expires on browser close, not an immediately invalid session. Do not interpret 0 as literal zero-second TTL in freshness tests.

Authenticator Validation stage 'Last validation threshold' uses a non-zero duration to suppress repeated MFA prompts. For code-based devices, values lower than seconds=30 cannot be used because exact timestamps are not available. For I3/I2 MFA-related tests, the fuzzer MUST avoid thresholds below 30 seconds when using TOTP/Static/SMS or it may misinterpret by-design caching behavior.

Email Authenticator Setup stage 'Token Expiration' is documented in minutes with default 30. Freshness tests involving email-based authenticators must account for this configured validity window rather than assuming immediate expiry semantics.

Email stage supports rate limiting via 'Account Recovery Max Attempts' and 'Account Recovery Cache Timeout'. If a test flow uses email verification or recovery as part of SAML-related setup, repeated attempts may be throttled by design. The fuzzer MUST avoid interpreting rate-limit failures as authentication freshness enforcement.

For I4 tests involving email-based linking or collision hypotheses, note that authentik documentation warns that email-based SAML NameID is mutable by default because users may change email addresses. A merge or relinking behavior driven by email-based NameID can be configuration-induced; tests should prefer persistent NameID formats when assessing principal binding robustness.

SAML provider/session logout behavior is session-tracking based. authentik creates SAMLSession records containing SessionIndex, NameID, and NameID format for successful authentications. Logout-related observations after administrative session deletion may reflect documented back-channel/front-channel SLO behavior rather than token/session confusion.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
